title: Kasut Kiri, Kasut Kanan
subject: a four-year-old who puts his tadika shoes on the wrong feet every morning until his mother sticks a cat on the left shoe and a fish on the right
caption: Malaysian children's sing-along in the lagu kanak-kanak style of preschool TV songs. A bright ukulele strumming steady eighth notes; a glockenspiel doubling the vocal melody note for note; short bright synth-brass stabs at the end of each line; hand claps and a shaker; a simple soft pop kit with a gentle kick and no heavy bass. Bright, clean and dry, ukulele and glockenspiel forward, every word clear and easy to follow. A friendly female adult lead, clearly enunciated and smiling, answered by a children's chorus singing the written replies. 116 BPM, G major. Bouncy, patient and silly. No sub-bass, no EDM drop, no trap hi-hats, no autotune, no club beat.
lyrics:
[Intro - ukulele strum and glockenspiel]

[Verse 1]
Pagi-pagi Adik bangun, nak pergi tadika
Beg dah siap, botol air dah isi
Duduk tepi pintu, sarung kasut sendiri
Eh, eh, kenapa jalan macam itik?

[Pre-Chorus]
Jom tengok kaki, jom kita kira
(Satu, dua!)

[Chorus]
Kasut kiri, kaki kiri
(Kiri! Kiri!)
Kasut kanan, kaki kanan
(Kanan! Kanan!)
Tepuk tangan, tukar balik
Baru boleh jalan laju

[Verse 2]
Malam tu Mak tampal sticker
Kasut kiri gambar kucing
Kasut kanan gambar ikan
Kucing pandang ikan, maknanya betul!

[Chorus]
Kasut kiri, kaki kiri
(Kiri! Kiri!)
Kasut kanan, kaki kanan
(Kanan! Kanan!)
Tepuk tangan, Adik pandai
Hari ni tak payah tukar

[Outro - glockenspiel and claps]
Satu, dua, tiga, jom pergi!
(Jom pergi!)
